writeup.headline: EOG rates Buy on strong growth, quality and trend, with valuation expensive against its own history.
writeup.thesis: EOG scores 78, a Buy, carried mainly by growth (92), quality (95) and trend (86). Latest-quarter revenue growth of 57.4% year on year and TTM revenue growth of 19.1% show growth sped up by 35.3 pp from the previous quarter. The operating margin is 33.0%, stock-based pay is 0.8% of revenue, and the diluted share count is down 3.1% year on year. The shares are 17.9% above their 200-day average and only 1.7% below their 52-week high. Valuation (58) holds the score back: P/S of 3.1x and EV/EBIT of 9.8x are moderate in absolute terms, but the stock is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S and more expensive than at 42 of the last 61 month-ends on EV/EBIT.
key_risks: Revenue and margins depend on crude and gas prices, so the sharp latest-quarter growth could reverse if prices fall.
Valuation is expensive against its own history on both P/S and EV/EBIT, leaving less cushion if results disappoint.
The shares sit near their 52-week high after a strong run, so a pullback could weaken the trend score.
Cash covers only 0.62 times debt, and the balance sheet could not be fully assessed.
Q3 results on Nov 5 could shift sentiment; the recent tax expense guidance raise was a mixed signal.
what_would_change: A gain of 2 points, for example from strong Q3 results or a better valuation score, would lift the rating to Strong Buy.
A drop of 14 points would move it to Hold, most likely through slowing growth alongside a weaker trend.
A fall in crude prices that cuts revenue growth and the operating margin would pull down the growth and quality scores.
Negative news on guidance or analyst downgrades would lower the news risk score from 54.
